backup_plan.description:
A reference to the BackupPlan from which Backups may be used
as the source for Restores created via this RestorePlan.
backup_plan.rationale: References the source BackupPlan used for restores. It is an external resource reference, so policy should not constrain team-specific BackupPlan names or IDs.

cluster.description: The name of the target cluster to which you want to Restore via this RestorePlan.
cluster.rationale: Identifier of the target cluster a restore writes to. It references another resource; we do not constrain which cluster a team restores into, and a generic policy cannot know a team's approved cluster names.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can delete or abandon the RestorePlan. Requiring deletion prevention reduces the risk of accidental or unauthorised removal.

description.description: User specified descriptive string for this RestorePlan.
description.rationale: Human-readable descriptive metadata only; it does not alter restore behaviour or security controls.

labels.description:
Description: A set of custom labels supplied by the user.
A list of key->value pairs.
Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: User-defined organisational metadata used for identification and management; labels do not directly control restore security behaviour.

location.description: The region of the Restore Plan.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description: The full name of the BackupPlan Resource.
name.rationale: Identifies the RestorePlan resource. Resource names are team-specific identifiers and are not security policy targets.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies the GCP project containing the RestorePlan. This is an external/project reference and should not be constrained by a generic resource policy.

restore_config.description: Defines the configuration of Restores created via this RestorePlan.

restore_config.all_namespaces.description:
If True, restore all namespaced resources in the Backup.
Setting this field to False will result in an error.
restore_config.all_namespaces.rationale: Controls whether resources from all namespaces are restored. Broad restoration can affect workloads across the cluster, so the restore scope should be explicitly constrained.

restore_config.cluster_resource_conflict.description:
Defines the behavior for handling the situation where cluster-scoped resources
being restored already exist in the target cluster.
This MUST be set to a value other than 'CLUSTER_RESOURCE_CONFLICT_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED'
if 'clusterResourceRestoreScope' is anyting other than 'noGroupKinds'.
See https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/add-on/backup-for-gke/reference/rest/v1/RestoreConfig#clusterresourceconflictpolicy
for more information on each policy option. Possible values: ["USE_EXISTING_VERSION", "USE_BACKUP_VERSION"]
restore_config.cluster_resource_conflict.rationale: Conflict policy should default to using existing versions to preserve state stability.

restore_config.namespaced_resource_resto.description:
Defines the behavior for handling the situation where sets of namespaced resources
being restored already exist in the target cluster.
This MUST be set to a value other than 'NAMESPACED_RESOURCE_RESTORE_MODE_UNSPECIFIED'
if the 'namespacedResourceRestoreScope' is anything other than 'noNamespaces'.
See https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/add-on/backup-for-gke/reference/rest/v1/RestoreConfig#namespacedresourcerestoremode
for more information on each mode. Possible values: ["DELETE_AND_RESTORE", "FAIL_ON_CONFLICT", "MERGE_SKIP_ON_CONFLICT", "MERGE_REPLACE_VOLUME_ON_CONFLICT", "MERGE_REPLACE_ON_CONFLICT"]
restore_config.namespaced_resource_resto.rationale: Determines how conflicts with existing namespaced resources are handled during restoration. Insecure conflict behaviour can overwrite or alter existing workloads.

restore_config.no_namespaces.description:
Do not restore any namespaced resources if set to "True".
Specifying this field to "False" is not allowed.
restore_config.no_namespaces.rationale: Controls whether namespaced resources are excluded entirely from restoration and therefore directly determines the scope of restored workloads.

restore_config.volume_data_restore_polic.description:
Specifies the mechanism to be used to restore volume data.
This should be set to a value other than 'NAMESPACED_RESOURCE_RESTORE_MODE_UNSPECIFIED'
if the 'namespacedResourceRestoreScope' is anything other than 'noNamespaces'.
If not specified, it will be treated as 'NO_VOLUME_DATA_RESTORATION'.
See https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/add-on/backup-for-gke/reference/rest/v1/RestoreConfig#VolumeDataRestorePolicy
for more information on each policy option. Possible values: ["RESTORE_VOLUME_DATA_FROM_BACKUP", "REUSE_VOLUME_HANDLE_FROM_BACKUP", "NO_VOLUME_DATA_RESTORATION"]
restore_config.volume_data_restore_polic.rationale: Controls whether volume data is restored, reused, or omitted. The selected behaviour can affect data integrity and exposure during recovery.

restore_config.cluster_resource_restore_.description: Identifies the cluster-scoped resources to restore from the Backup.

If True, all valid cluster-scoped resources will be restored.
Mutually exclusive to any other field in 'clusterResourceRestoreScope'.
restore_config.cluster_resource_restore_.rationale: Avoid full cluster restores to prevent overwriting critical existing resources unless explicitly intended.

restore_config.cluster_resource_restore_.description:
If True, no cluster-scoped resources will be restored.
Mutually exclusive to any other field in 'clusterResourceRestoreScope'.
restore_config.cluster_resource_restore_.rationale: Controls whether cluster-scoped resources are excluded from restoration and therefore directly limits the scope and impact of a restore.

restore_config.cluster_resource_restore_.description:
A list of cluster-scoped resource group kinds to NOT restore from the backup.
If specified, all valid cluster-scoped resources will be restored except
for those specified in the list.
Mutually exclusive to any other field in 'clusterResourceRestoreScope'.

API Group string of a Kubernetes resource, e.g.
"apiextensions.k8s.io", "storage.k8s.io", etc.
Use empty string for core group.
restore_config.cluster_resource_restore_.rationale: Determines which Kubernetes API groups are excluded from a cluster-resource restore, affecting the security-sensitive restore scope.

restore_config.cluster_resource_restore_.description:
Kind of a Kubernetes resource, e.g.
"CustomResourceDefinition", "StorageClass", etc.
restore_config.cluster_resource_restore_.rationale: Determines which Kubernetes resource kinds are excluded from restoration and can prevent sensitive cluster resources from being overwritten.

restore_config.cluster_resource_restore_.description:
A list of cluster-scoped resource group kinds to restore from the backup.
If specified, only the selected resources will be restored.
Mutually exclusive to any other field in the 'clusterResourceRestoreScope'.

API Group string of a Kubernetes resource, e.g.
"apiextensions.k8s.io", "storage.k8s.io", etc.
Use empty string for core group.
restore_config.cluster_resource_restore_.rationale: Defines Kubernetes API groups explicitly selected for restoration and therefore controls the scope of cluster-level changes.

restore_config.cluster_resource_restore_.description:
Kind of a Kubernetes resource, e.g.
"CustomResourceDefinition", "StorageClass", etc.
restore_config.cluster_resource_restore_.rationale: Defines Kubernetes resource kinds explicitly selected for restoration and therefore controls which cluster resources may be modified.

restore_config.excluded_namespaces.description:
A list of selected namespaces excluded from restoration.
All namespaces except those in this list will be restored.

restore_config.excluded_namespaces.names.rationale: Specifies namespaces that must not be restored. This can protect sensitive or operational namespaces from unintended modification.

restore_config.restore_order.description: It contains custom ordering to use on a Restore.

restore_config.restore_order.group_kind_.description:
A list of group kind dependency pairs
that is used by Backup for GKE to
generate a group kind restore order.

The requiring group kind requires that the satisfying
group kind be restored first.

API Group of a Kubernetes resource, e.g.
"apiextensions.k8s.io", "storage.k8s.io", etc.
Use empty string for core group.
restore_config.restore_order.group_kind_.rationale: Identifies the API group participating in a custom restore dependency. It describes ordering rather than enforcing a security boundary.

restore_config.restore_order.group_kind_.description:
Kind of a Kubernetes resource, e.g.
"CustomResourceDefinition", "StorageClass", etc.
restore_config.restore_order.group_kind_.rationale: Identifies a Kubernetes resource kind in the custom restore order; this is dependency/order configuration rather than a generic security constraint.

restore_config.restore_order.group_kind_.description:
The satisfying group kind must be restored first
in order to satisfy the dependency.

API Group of a Kubernetes resource, e.g.
"apiextensions.k8s.io", "storage.k8s.io", etc.
Use empty string for core group.
restore_config.restore_order.group_kind_.rationale: Identifies the API group that must be restored first. It controls dependency ordering rather than a security minimum.

restore_config.restore_order.group_kind_.description:
Kind of a Kubernetes resource, e.g.
"CustomResourceDefinition", "StorageClass", etc.
restore_config.restore_order.group_kind_.rationale: Identifies the resource kind satisfying a restore dependency and is primarily restore sequencing configuration.

restore_config.selected_applications.description:
A list of selected ProtectedApplications to restore.
The listed ProtectedApplications and all the resources
to which they refer will be restored.

restore_config.selected_applications.nam.description: A list of namespaced Kubernetes resources.
The name of a Kubernetes Resource.
restore_config.selected_applications.nam.rationale: Identifies a specific Kubernetes application/resource to restore. Application names are deployment-specific and should not be constrained generically.

restore_config.selected_applications.nam.description: The namespace of a Kubernetes Resource.
restore_config.selected_applications.nam.rationale: Determines the namespace from which a selected application is restored, directly affecting which namespace and workloads are within restore scope.

restore_config.selected_namespaces.description:
A list of selected namespaces to restore from the Backup.
The listed Namespaces and all resources contained in them will be restored.

restore_config.selected_namespaces.names.rationale: Explicitly determines which namespaces and contained resources are restored, making it a security-relevant restore-scope control.

restore_config.transformation_rules.description:
A list of transformation rules to be applied against Kubernetes
resources as they are selected for restoration from a Backup.
Rules are executed in order defined - this order matters,
as changes made by a rule may impact the filtering logic of subsequent
rules. An empty list means no transformation will occur.

restore_config.transformation_rules.desc.description:
The description is a user specified string description
of the transformation rule.
restore_config.transformation_rules.desc.rationale: Descriptive metadata for a transformation rule and does not itself modify restored resources.

restore_config.transformation_rules.fiel.description:
A list of transformation rule actions to take against candidate
resources. Actions are executed in order defined - this order
matters, as they could potentially interfere with each other and
the first operation could affect the outcome of the second operation.

A string containing a JSON Pointer value that references the
location in the target document to move the value from.
restore_config.transformation_rules.fiel.rationale: Selects the source field used by transformation operations such as MOVE or COPY, affecting what data/configuration can be changed during restore.

restore_config.transformation_rules.fiel.description: Specifies the operation to perform. Possible values: ["REMOVE", "MOVE", "COPY", "ADD", "TEST", "REPLACE"]
restore_config.transformation_rules.fiel.rationale: Determines the transformation operation performed against restored resources. Operations such as REMOVE, ADD or REPLACE can materially change security-relevant configuration.

restore_config.transformation_rules.fiel.description:
A string containing a JSON-Pointer value that references a
location within the target document where the operation is performed.
restore_config.transformation_rules.fiel.rationale: Specifies the target field modified by a transformation action and can therefore affect security-sensitive resource configuration.

restore_config.transformation_rules.fiel.description:
A string that specifies the desired value in string format
to use for transformation.
restore_config.transformation_rules.fiel.rationale: Supplies the replacement or added value used by transformation actions and can change security-relevant configuration during restoration.

restore_config.transformation_rules.reso.description:
This field is used to specify a set of fields that should be used to
determine which resources in backup should be acted upon by the
supplied transformation rule actions, and this will ensure that only
specific resources are affected by transformation rule actions.

This is a JSONPath expression that matches specific fields of
candidate resources and it operates as a filtering parameter
(resources that are not matched with this expression will not
be candidates for transformation).
restore_config.transformation_rules.reso.rationale: Controls which resource fields qualify for transformation. An overly broad filter can cause security-sensitive changes to unintended resources.

restore_config.transformation_rules.reso.description:
(Filtering parameter) Any resource subject to transformation must
be contained within one of the listed Kubernetes Namespace in the
Backup. If this field is not provided, no namespace filtering will
be performed (all resources in all Namespaces, including all
cluster-scoped resources, will be candidates for transformation).
To mix cluster-scoped and namespaced resources in the same rule,
use an empty string ("") as one of the target namespaces.
restore_config.transformation_rules.reso.rationale: Limits transformation rules to specified namespaces. Without appropriate scope, transformations can affect resources across multiple namespaces.

restore_config.transformation_rules.reso.description:
(Filtering parameter) Any resource subject to transformation must
belong to one of the listed "types". If this field is not provided,
no type filtering will be performed
(all resources of all types matching previous filtering parameters
will be candidates for transformation).

API Group string of a Kubernetes resource, e.g.
"apiextensions.k8s.io", "storage.k8s.io", etc.
Use empty string for core group.
restore_config.transformation_rules.reso.rationale: Restricts transformation rules by Kubernetes API group and therefore controls which resource types can be modified during restoration.

restore_config.transformation_rules.reso.description:
Kind of a Kubernetes resource, e.g.
"CustomResourceDefinition", "StorageClass", etc.
restore_config.transformation_rules.reso.rationale: Restricts transformation rules to particular Kubernetes resource kinds and therefore limits the security impact of transformations.

restore_config.volume_data_restore_polic.description:
A table that binds volumes by their scope to a restore policy. Bindings
must have a unique scope. Any volumes not scoped in the bindings are
subject to the policy defined in volume_data_restore_policy.

Specifies the mechanism to be used to restore this volume data.
See https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/add-on/backup-for-gke/reference/rest/v1/RestoreConfig#VolumeDataRestorePolicy
for more information on each policy option. Possible values: ["RESTORE_VOLUME_DATA_FROM_BACKUP", "REUSE_VOLUME_HANDLE_FROM_BACKUP", "NO_VOLUME_DATA_RESTORATION"]
restore_config.volume_data_restore_polic.rationale: Determines how volume data within the binding is restored, reused or omitted, directly affecting restored data integrity and handling.

restore_config.volume_data_restore_polic.description:
The volume type, as determined by the PVC's
bound PV, to apply the policy to. Possible values: ["GCE_PERSISTENT_DISK"]
restore_config.volume_data_restore_polic.rationale: Identifies the volume technology to which a binding applies. The supported volume type is provider-defined rather than a security policy choice.
